description: Intelligent Driver Model with a Matérn-5/2 Gaussian-process noise structure on velocity-prediction residuals (IDM+GP). Adapted from the published Bayesian framework — Chengyuan Zhang, Lijun Sun, 'Bayesian Calibration of the Intelligent Driver Model' (arXiv 2210.03571).
assumptions: Pooled population IDM parameters. Acceleration clipped to [-10, 5] m/s^2. Residual eps_t (m/s) follows a zero-mean GP with Matérn-5/2 kernel K(t,t') = sigma_f^2 * (1 + sqrt(5)|tau|/ell + 5 tau^2/(3 ell^2)) * exp(-sqrt(5)|tau|/ell), plus diagonal noise sigma_n^2 * I. At test time, future residuals are drawn from the GP conditional posterior given up to 28 most recent observed history residuals.
calibration: Two-stage calibration on OpenCF train.csv (Waymo, dt=0.1, urban: q99 follower_speed = 19.6 m/s). Stage 1 (IDM): differential-evolution closed-loop velocity-RMSE fit over 30-step (3.0 s) rollouts on 4,000 random pairs, urban-typical bounds (v0 in [15,30], T in [0.6,2.5], a in [0.5,3], b in [0.5,3], s0 in [1,4]). Result: v0=28.46, T=0.99, a=1.31, b=0.54, s0=3.29 (delta=4 fixed). Stage 2 (Matérn-5/2 hyperparameters): marginal-likelihood (ML-II) fit on IDM residuals from 2,000 pairs split into 3,002 fixed-length chunks. Result: ell=0.817, sigma_f=0.0779, sigma_n=0.0171. PyMC NUTS pooled joint inference (800 pairs, 1,500 chunks, 2 chains x (500 tune + 500 draws), prior-scale=0.3 anchored at the DE point) was also explored but the joint one-step-prediction likelihood pulls IDM into a regime where the flexible GP residual absorbs short-term dynamics, hurting the closed-loop trajectory metric — the DE-anchored two-stage fit was retained for the final submission. At inference, 6 trajectories per pair are simulated using the calibrated IDM with independent draws from the GP conditional posterior on each pair's last 28 history residuals.
